cases.sentence: ___, всегда державший огромную охоту, теперь же передавший всю охоту в ведение сына, в этот день, 15-го сентября, развеселившись, собрался сам тоже выехать.
cases.explain: «Старый граф» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The old count, who had always kept up an enormous hunting establishment but had now handed it all completely over to his son’s care, being in very good spirits on this fifteenth of September, prepared to go out with the others.

cases.sentence: Лошадь ___, игреневого меренка, называемого Вифлянкой, вел графский стремянной; сам же он должен был прямо выехать в дрожечках на оставленный ему лаз.
cases.explain: «старого графа» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: In an hour’s time the whole hunting party was at the porch. Nikoláy, with a stern and serious air which showed that now was no time for attending to trifles, went past Natásha and Pétya who were trying to tell him something. He had a look at all the details of the hunt, sent a pack of hounds and huntsmen on ahead to find the quarry, mounted his chestnut Donéts, and whistling to his own leash of borzois, set off across the threshing ground to a field leading to the Otrádnoe wood. The old count’s horse, a sorrel gelding called Viflyánka, was led by the groom in attendance on him, while the count himself was to drive in a small trap straight to a spot reserved for him.

cases.sentence: Борзятников кроме господ было 8 человек, за которыми рыскало более 40 борзых, так что с ___ выехало в поле около 130-ти собак и 20-ти конных охотников.
cases.explain: «господскими сворами» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: They were taking fifty-four hounds, with six hunt attendants and whippers-in. Besides the family, there were eight borzoi kennelmen and more than forty borzois, so that, with the borzois on the leash belonging to members of the family, there were about a hundred and thirty dogs and twenty horsemen.

cases.sentence: Как только вышли за ограду, все без шуму и разговоров равномерно и спокойно растянулись по дороге и полю, ведшими к ___.
cases.explain: «Отрадненскому лесу» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: Each dog knew its master and its call. Each man in the hunt knew his business, his place, what he had to do. As soon as they had passed the fence they all spread out evenly and quietly, without noise or talk, along the road and field leading to the Otrádnoe covert.

cases.sentence: Как по ___ шли по полю лошади, изредка шлепая по лужам, когда переходили через дороги.
cases.explain: «пушному ковру» — after the preposition «по», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: The horses stepped over the field as over a thick carpet, now and then splashing into puddles as they crossed a road. The misty sky still seemed to descend evenly and imperceptibly toward the earth, the air was still, warm, and silent. Occasionally the whistle of a huntsman, the snort of a horse, the crack of a whip, or the whine of a straggling hound could be heard.

cases.sentence: ___ продолжало незаметно и равномерно спускаться на землю; в воздухе было тихо, тепло, беззвучно.
cases.explain: «Туманное небо» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The horses stepped over the field as over a thick carpet, now and then splashing into puddles as they crossed a road. The misty sky still seemed to descend evenly and imperceptibly toward the earth, the air was still, warm, and silent. Occasionally the whistle of a huntsman, the snort of a horse, the crack of a whip, or the whine of a straggling hound could be heard.

cases.sentence: Когда отъехали с версту, навстречу ___ из тумана показалось еще пять всадников с собаками.
cases.explain: «Ростовской охоте» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: When they had gone a little less than a mile, five more riders with dogs appeared out of the mist, approaching the Rostóvs. In front rode a fresh-looking, handsome old man with a large gray mustache.

cases.sentence: Впереди ехал свежий, красивый старик с большими ___.
cases.explain: «седыми усами» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: When they had gone a little less than a mile, five more riders with dogs appeared out of the mist, approaching the Rostóvs. In front rode a fresh-looking, handsome old man with a large gray mustache.

cases.sentence: Так и знал, — заговорил дядюшка (это был ___, небогатый сосед Ростовых), — так и знал, что не вытерпишь, и хорошо, что едешь.
cases.explain: «дальний родственник» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “That’s it. Come on! … I was sure of it,” began “Uncle.” (He was a distant relative of the Rostóvs’, a man of small means, and their neighbor.) “I knew you wouldn’t be able to resist it and it’s a good thing you’re going. That’s it! Come on!” (This was “Uncle’s” favorite expression.) “Take the covert at once, for my Gírchik says the Ilágins are at Kornikí with their hounds. That’s it. Come on! … They’ll take the cubs from under your very nose.”

cases.sentence: Карай был старый и уродливый, бурдастый кобель, известный тем, что он в одиночку бирал ___.
cases.explain: «матерого волка» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “That’s as may happen,” answered Rostóv. “Karáy, here!” he shouted, answering “Uncle’s” remark by this call to his borzoi. Karáy was a shaggy old dog with a hanging jowl, famous for having tackled a big wolf unaided. They all took up their places.
